submission.justification: R1 gives the best separation (4.56 sigma at 3 cm). However, it is a porous radiator with no hydrophobic treatment, and no document gives lifetime or aging data for any candidate. The dry-nitrogen flush only helps during operation. R2 is the best candidate that has a documented protection against moisture, which is the likely aging mechanism for porous radiators. R2 separation peaks at about 3 cm (3.65 sigma) and falls at larger thickness. This is a trade-off: it costs about 0.9 sigma against R1. If the collaboration can confirm that R1 stays stable under the dry-N2 flush, R1 at 3 cm would be the better choice. R3 is lower in performance (2.9 sigma at 3 cm in the 2025 summary) and I did not re-simulate it.

requirements.requirement: Best possible pi/K separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R2 at 3 cm gives 3.65 sigma. R1 gives 4.56 sigma at 3 cm, so I gave up about 0.9 sigma for lifetime safety.

requirements.requirement: Radiator is one of the three candidates
Performance kept over the experiment lifetime
requirements.evidence: No aging data exists. R2 has a hydrophobic treatment, and the vessel is flushed with dry N2. R1 has no documented protection.
